Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

3. Tolerances on Bandsaw Blades 

3.1 Tooth Set Tolerances — The overall set is left to the manufacturer's discretion. The set at each 
side of the blade shall be equal and maintained within the limits of ±005 mm or ±0'10 mm overall. 

3.2 Flatness Tolerance — The blade shall be flat across the sectional profile exclusive of set, within 
the tolerances as specified beiow: 



CROSS-SECTIONAL 
.PROFILE OF BLADE

IS: 5030 (Part ll)-1982 

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

While revising IS : 5030-1969 'Flexible-back metal cutting bandsaw blades', it has been split up 
into the following three parts: 

Part 1 Definitions and terminology. 

Part II Tolerances. 

Part III Dimensions and requirements. 

This standard Part II specifies the various tolerances as applicable to bandsaw blades. 

Different methods of indicating the size of teeth are used in different countries, such as 

specifying pitch of teeth in millimetres, number of teeth per 25 mm or number of teeth per inch or 

both. In this standard the pitch of teeth is given in millimetres and a tolerance is allowed on the 
same. 

This part is based on ISO 4875/11-1978 'Metal cutting band saw blades — Part II : Basic 
dimensions and tolerances' issued by Internationa! Organization for Standardization. 



Printed at Printrade, New Delhi, India
